question: Which of the following States is a part of Panjnad (land of five rivers)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Punjab is known as the land of five rivers: Beas, Ravi, Sutlej, Chenab, and Jhelum.
 
• The name "Punjab" is derived from the Persian words "panj" (five) and "ab" (water), referring to the five major rivers in the region.
 
• The five rivers contribute significantly to the agricultural fertility of the state, making Punjab one of the most prosperous agricultural regions in India.
 
• These rivers eventually merge to form the Panjnad, which is a point where all five rivers combine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Beas River**

 
 
• The Beas River is one of the five rivers of Punjab and flows through the states of Himachal Pradesh and Punjab.
 
• It is known for its historical significance as it marked the eastern extent of Alexander the Great's invasion in 326 BCE.
 
 
 
• **Ravi River**
 
 
• The Ravi River flows through the Indian state of Punjab and the Pakistani province of Punjab.
 
• It is one of the major tributaries of the Indus River system.
 
 
 
• **Sutlej River**
 
 
• The Sutlej River is the longest of the five rivers of Punjab.
 
• It originates from Lake Rakshastal in Tibet and flows through Himachal Pradesh and Punjab before entering Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Chenab River**
 
 
• The Chenab River flows through the Indian state of Jammu and Kashmir and the Pakistani province of Punjab.
 
• It is a major river of the Indus River system, and it merges with the Jhelum and Sutlej rivers in Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Jhelum River**
 
 
• The Jhelum River flows through the Indian-administered territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Pakistani province of Punjab.
 
• It is notable for its scenic beauty and historical importance as it passes through the Kashmir Valley.
